title: Arizona’s Apache trout neared extinction; after recovery, a new barrier protects 22 miles of habitat
summary_full: Arizona's Apache trout has seen a stunning recovery from the brink of extinction, largely due to the proactive conservation efforts spearheaded by the White Mountain Apache Tribe. Officially taken off the list of federally protected species in September 2024, this fish now thrives in its natural habitat, shielded from invasive trout by a newly erected barrier. Ongoing management and monitoring of the species are essential for ensuring its long-term survival.
